parameters.content:
## Find and fix broken links in YouTube descriptions and comments

Dead affiliate links, expired discount codes and moved pages under old videos quietly cost creators clicks and revenue. This workflow finds them every week and lets you fix them from Slack without opening YouTube Studio.

### How it works
1. Every Monday it lists every video and Short on your channel and reads each description plus the comments you posted yourself.
2. Each unique link is checked once. Besides 404s and dead domains, it catches **soft 404s** (pages that load but say "no longer available") and links that **redirect to the homepage**.
3. A Data Table remembers every issue, so you're only asked about new ones, and you're told when a link works again.
4. For each new broken link, Slack asks what to do. Choose **Replace link** and enter the new URL to rewrite it in every description and comment where it appears, or **Ignore this link** to stop alerts. No answer within 7 days? You're asked again the next week.
5. A weekly email lists every open issue.

### Setup
1. Create a Data Table named **YouTube Link Issues** with the text columns `url`, `status`, `reason` and `replacement`.
2. Connect **YouTube OAuth2**, **Slack** and **SMTP** credentials.
3. Fill in **Configuration**: uploads playlist ID (your channel ID with `UC` replaced by `UU`), sender and report emails, Slack channel ID.
4. Publish the workflow, since fix requests run as separate executions of it.

### Customization
- Edit the soft-404 phrases in **Configuration**.
- Change which status codes count as broken in **Classify Result**.

Only the first 100 comment threads per video are read, and translated descriptions keep the old link.


Built by
[![Cloud Labs](https://low-code-consultant.com/brand/n8n-strip.png#full-width)](https://low-code-consultant.com)

## 1. Collect links
Your settings, the links already tracked, and every link in your descriptions and in comments you posted, grouped by URL.

## 2. Check each link
Catches errors, soft 404s and redirects to the homepage, then compares with known issues.

## 3. Act on results
Links that work again are marked fixed and announced in Slack. New issues are recorded, and each new broken link gets a fix request. One weekly email lists every open issue.

## 4. Ask for a fix
Runs once per new broken link and waits up to 7 days for an answer in Slack. Without a valid answer, it asks again next week.

## 5. Rewrite the link
Replaces the link in every description and comment, records the result and confirms in Slack.
